description: Detailed host metrics for the macOS host. Every panel is built against a metric this exporter actually publishes, verified against its live metric list. The two update panels require a textfile collector script and are marked as such.

panels.description: Short uptime after an alert means a crash, not a planned restart.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description: Sanity check that the exporter is reading this machine. Expect 16 GiB.
panels.title: Memory total

panels.description: Needed to interpret the load average.
panels.title: CPU cores

panels.description: Clock drift breaks TLS validation, token expiry and log correlation.
panels.title: Clock skew

panels.description: A failed collector leaves part of this dashboard empty while the exporter still reports up.
panels.title: Collectors failing

panels.description: 1 means a .prom file is malformed or the directory is unreadable, for example when the external SSD is unmounted.
panels.title: Textfile errors

panels.description: Load is runnable processes, not CPU percent. Divide by the core count to compare against CPU busy.
panels.title: Load average

panels.description: Hostname, kernel release and architecture. node_os_version carries the macOS version number.
panels.title: System information

panels.description: Busy is 100 minus idle. The 5m range is 20x the 15s scrape interval.
panels.title: CPU busy

panels.description: Darwin reports user, system and nice only. No iowait or steal, so disk waits hide inside system time.
panels.title: CPU by mode

panels.description: Spots a single pinned core that an average would hide. The M4 has performance and efficiency cores, so uneven load is normal.
panels.title: CPU per core

panels.description: The honest macOS view. A used-percent gauge is misleading here because free excludes cache.
panels.title: Memory breakdown

panels.description: The best macOS pressure signal. Rising compression means the system is squeezing RAM before it swaps.
panels.title: Compressed memory

panels.description: Wired cannot be paged out. Internal is application memory. Purgeable can be reclaimed on demand.
panels.title: Memory by category

panels.description: Memory held by applications rather than the kernel or cache. A steady climb here is an application leak; a climb in wired is a kernel or driver leak.
panels.title: Application memory

panels.description: Cannot be paged out, so it sets a floor under everything else. Kernel extensions and drivers live here.
panels.title: Wired memory

panels.description: clamp_min guards against division by zero when macOS has not created a swap file yet.
panels.title: Swap used

panels.description: macOS grows the swap file on demand, so the total rising is itself a pressure signal.
panels.title: Swap used and total

panels.description: Counters, so they need rate(). Sustained swap-out is real pressure; a brief spike is not.
panels.title: Swap activity

panels.description: Every volume including the external SSD. 85 matches the alert threshold so dashboard and alert agree. Filtered to the data volume and external mounts: /, Preboot, Update and VM share one APFS container and report identical numbers, and /System/Volumes/Data/home is a zero-size automount that would divide by zero.
panels.title: Disk used percent

panels.description: Thresholds are 20 GiB and 50 GiB. Filtered to the data volume and external mounts: /, Preboot, Update and VM share one APFS container and report identical numbers, and /System/Volumes/Data/home is a zero-size automount that would divide by zero.
panels.title: Free space by volume

panels.description: macOS only. Finder counts purgeable as available, df does not, which is why the two disagree about free space. Filtered to the data volume and external mounts: /, Preboot, Update and VM share one APFS container and report identical numbers, and /System/Volumes/Data/home is a zero-size automount that would divide by zero.
panels.title: Purgeable space

panels.description: Negative means filling. Adjust the mountpoint if your exporter labels it differently.
panels.title: Days until internal volume is full

panels.description: Rare on APFS, but it is how 'disk full with space free' actually presents.
panels.title: Inodes free

panels.description: A device error or a volume flipping to read only is a serious failure that nothing else on this dashboard would show. APFS mounts read only when it detects corruption.
panels.title: Volume health

panels.description: Internal drive and external SSD reported separately.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Operations per second. Throughput and IOPS tell different stories about the same workload.
panels.title: IOPS

panels.description: Average seconds per operation. Rising latency at flat throughput means the device is struggling, which is early evidence of a failing drive.
panels.title: Latency per operation

panels.description: Hardware health. Retries rise before errors do, so this is the earliest warning of a failing drive. Almost no dashboard shows it.
panels.title: Disk errors and retries, last 1h

panels.description: Sector counts rather than bytes. Dividing by the IOPS panel gives the average request size.
panels.title: Sectors moved

panels.description: The filter removes loopback, VPN tunnels, Apple Wireless Direct Link and bridges, which otherwise dominate the legend.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Packet rate and byte rate diverge when packet sizes change.
panels.title: Packets per second

panels.description: Sustained errors point at interference, a cable or a driver. Relevant given the ICMP flapping already observed on this network.
panels.title: Errors, drops and collisions, last 1h

panels.description: Heavy multicast is normal on a home network with discovery protocols. A rise in unknown protocol traffic is not.
panels.title: Multicast and unknown protocol
Software updates (requires a textfile collector script)

panels.description: Not exported by node_exporter. Needs a textfile script running softwareupdate -l --no-scan. Shows No data until that is in place.
panels.title: Pending macOS updates

panels.description: Catches the silent failure where the script stopped running and zero pending looks identical to healthy.
panels.title: Update check age

panels.description: 1 means a .prom file is malformed or the directory is unreadable. Without this panel that failure is invisible.
panels.title: Textfile collector health

panels.description: 1 means the collector ran. 0 explains an empty panel elsewhere on this dashboard.
panels.title: Collectors

panels.description: A slow collector lengthens every scrape.
panels.title: Collector duration

panels.description: The monitoring agent should not become the problem it reports on.
panels.title: Exporter resources

panels.description: A restarting exporter produces gaps that look like host problems.
panels.title: Exporter CPU and uptime

panels.description: Running out of descriptors breaks the exporter in a way that looks like a network problem.
panels.title: File descriptors

panels.description: Errors serving the metrics endpoint itself. Requests in flight stuck above zero means a scrape is hanging.
panels.title: Scrape handler errors

title: Mac host detail
